## Automation / wiring summary
- Change type: modify existing prompt files only.
- Scheduler / PR-push wiring: none.
- New supervisor: none.
- DB gate pattern: none.
- `docs/scripts-pending-removal.md` entry: none.

## Scope summary
Use `prompts/mode-implement.txt` as the canonical prompt, then add only short cross-references in the diagnose/repair trio. This fits the issue’s “one prompt family, one rollout” budget and avoids duplicating the full rule set.

## Files likely to change
1. `prompts/mode-implement.txt`
   - Current relevant areas:
     - conflict-detection block at lines 12-14
     - restriction block at lines 21-24
     - dependency/lockfile discipline at lines 32-40
     - data-file output discipline starts at line 42
   - Planned edits:
     - narrow the blanket governance-doc ban so `ai_pipeline.md` stays forbidden, while `unattended_system_instructions.md` / `CLAUDE.md` become editable only when explicitly named by the approved plan or `files_touched` scope
     - add the new `Plan-divergence discipline` paragraph immediately after the conflict-detection block
     - add the `Code-style hints` subsection between dependency/lockfile discipline and data-file output discipline

2. `prompts/mode-implement-diagnose.txt`
   - Insert a short plan-divergence cross-reference near the policy section, most naturally after `Self-contained fix-up` and before `Output contract`.

3. `prompts/mode-implement-repair.txt`
   - Insert the same short cross-reference after the scope/allow-list paragraph and before `Category-specific repair recipes`.

4. `prompts/mode-implement-repair-syntax.txt`
   - Insert the same short cross-reference after `Validation target` and before `Category-specific repair recipes`.

No files should be created, deleted, or renamed.

## Functions / modules to implement
No runtime functions are involved; this is prompt-contract work. The implementer should update these prompt modules/sections:

- `mode-implement.txt`
  - governance-doc restriction wording
  - new `Plan-divergence discipline` prose
  - new `Code-style hints` prose:
    - descriptive naming
    - no inline comments unless requested or the “why” is non-obvious
    - implementation flow: discovery → note divergence → batch edits → reconcile → final summary

- diagnose/repair trio
  - add a short cross-reference back to the canonical rule in `prompts/mode-implement.txt`
  - do not duplicate the full Phase 4 prose

## Data structures affected
- No runtime data structures, schemas, env vars, or APIs change.
- The only structured artifact in scope is the existing JSON schema text in `prompts/mode-implement-diagnose.txt`; it must remain unchanged.
- Effective contract change is behavioral: the implement-family prompts will now explicitly require surfacing material plan/codebase divergence and will narrowly permit governance-doc edits only when explicitly in scope.

## API / interface changes
- No external API changes.
- No CLI, workflow, or env-var interface changes.
- Internal prompt-interface change only:
  - implementation prompt becomes less absolute about `unattended_system_instructions.md` / `CLAUDE.md`, but only behind explicit scope gates
  - diagnose/repair prompts gain a canonical-reference rule for divergence handling

## Conflict notes
1. The source-of-truth Phase 6 wording talks about surfacing plan divergence in output, but `prompts/mode-implement-diagnose.txt` currently requires exactly one JSON object and forbids extra text. The implementation must preserve that schema and surface divergence inside existing JSON fields/body text rather than inventing a new field or free-text line.
2. `prompts/mode-implement.txt` currently has no markdown subsection headings; “add a subsection” should be implemented as a local titled prose block, not a broader format refactor.

## Risks / edge cases
- The narrowed restriction must not create a general self-modifying loophole:
  - `ai_pipeline.md` remains always forbidden
  - `unattended_system_instructions.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are only allowed when explicitly named in the approved plan or explicit `files_touched` scope
  - no broad “governance docs” wording
- Preserve existing placeholders/tokens verbatim:
  - `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}` in all four files
  - `{{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION}}` in `mode-implement.txt`
- Preserve existing output-contract/schema text, especially:
  - `Output: repository changes only.`
  - the JSON schema block in `mode-implement-diagnose.txt`
- Keep edits additive/local; do not rename headings, placeholders, or surrounding policy labels.
- Stay inside the four-file scope only; do not touch `unattended_system_instructions.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `prompts/review-reviewer-checklist.txt` in this issue.

## Testing / verification considerations
- `git diff --name-only` should show only:
  - `prompts/mode-implement.txt`
  - `prompts/mode-implement-diagnose.txt`
  - `prompts/mode-implement-repair.txt`
  - `prompts/mode-implement-repair-syntax.txt`
- `git diff --check` for whitespace/regression hygiene.
- Grep verification:
  - `{{SERENA_TOOL_HINTS}}` still present in all four files
  - `{{WORKFLOW_EDIT_RESTRICTION}}` still present in `mode-implement.txt`
  - new `Code-style hints` block present in `mode-implement.txt`
  - new `Plan-divergence discipline` text present in all required files
  - restriction text still leaves `ai_pipeline.md` forbidden and scopes the `unattended_system_instructions.md` / `CLAUDE.md` exception
- Manual diff review to confirm no output-contract/schema wording was removed or renamed.

## Assumptions
- This issue only changes prompt text; no downstream parser/workflow changes are needed here.
- The scoped allowance can rely on the existing approved-plan / `files_touched` concepts already referenced by the implement prompt family.
